drafts.type: behind the work (my site vs client sites)
drafts.text:
My own site has a 3D robot on it, so it scores lower on Google's speed test than the sites I build for clients.

That's on purpose. My site is where I show off design.

A client site has one job. Load fast and get the phone to ring. My sister's electrician site scores 99-100.

drafts.text:
Space heater season is coming.

Plug it straight into a wall outlet. Skip the extension cord and the power strip.

A heater pulls a lot of current. A thin cord pushes back with resistance, and that turns into heat in the cord. That's how cords melt and fires start.
drafts.pattern: Plain-English take on a physics explainer (electric_4u 'What exactly is electrical resistance?', 3.6k, 17 bookmarks) turned into a homeowner do-this rule
drafts.video_tip: 5 seconds: a space heater cord going straight into a wall outlet, with a power strip pushed aside.
drafts.best_time_ct: electric_4u's explainer went out at 1:39 AM CT, so still no useful electrician timing. Homeowner tips: evenings or Saturday morning are a guess, not data.

drafts.type: safety tip (lights dim when AC kicks on)
drafts.text:
Lights dim for a second when the AC or fridge kicks on?

A quick dip can be normal when a big motor starts.

If they flicker a lot, stay dim, or it's getting worse, that can be a loose connection. Have a licensed electrician check it.
drafts.pattern: Question opener with a clear when-to-worry answer (evergreen homeowner explainer)
